method: Python: traverse uv.lock from the paperdesk runtime, build, and dev roots; evaluate dependency markers for CPython 3.12 on Windows; read installed wheel METADATA License-Expression/License fields and inspect named local LICENSE files where needed.

JavaScript: traverse pnpm-lock.yaml snapshots from production and development importer roots, including optional edges; read license values from the exact installed package.json. A missing installed package or license declaration is recorded as unknown.

pnpm licenses list --prod --json groups by package name: it shows 274 grouped records covering 282 exact name/version pairs. The lock traversal has 295 production pairs: 285 installed for Windows x64 and 10 optional binaries for other OS/CPU combinations that were not installed. The pnpm license command omits three installed production pairs listed in summary; their package.json files were inspected directly and declare MIT.

Rust: run cargo tree --locked --offline --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (and --edges normal), then read the exact-version cached Cargo.toml package.license. Other-platform entries in Cargo.lock are excluded.

A production or normal-graph reachability flag means dependency graph inclusion, not proof that code survives tree shaking or appears in the released binary. Inspect final build artifacts separately before publication.
License strings are kept as declared upstream, rather than silently normalized to a different SPDX expression. Unknown means this audit did not verify a license for that locked version.

All 66 unknown JavaScript licenses belong to optional binaries for other OS/CPU combinations absent from the audit machine (10 production, 56 development). The two unknown Python licenses are also other-platform packages absent on Windows. The Windows x64 dependency rows audited from installed metadata have no unknown licenses.
